quotes.t: Although you may spend your life killing, you will not exhaust all your foes. But if you quell your own anger, your real enemy will be slain.
quotes.c: Prajñadanda (The Staff of Wisdom), Elegant Sayings: Nagarjuna's Staff of Wisdom & Sakya Pandit's Treasury of Elegant Sayings (Cazadero, CA: Dharma Publishing, 1977), pp. 38, 48

quotes.t: If you desire ease, forsake learning. If you desire learning, forsake ease.How can the man at his ease acquire knowledge, And how can the earnest student enjoy ease?
"I am not, I will not be. I have not, I will not have." That frightens all the childish And extinguishes fear in the wise.
"I, without grasping will pass beyond sorrow, And I will attain nirvāṇa," one says. Whoever grasps like this Has great grasping.
Due to having faith one relies on the practices, Due to having wisdom one truly knows. Of these two wisdom is the chief, Faith is its prerequisite.
quotes.c: Ratnāvalī (Precious Garland), The Precious Garland, 5 trans. by Jeffrey Hopkins, "Buddhist Advice for Living and Liberation: Nagarjuna's Precious Garland" (1998)

quotes.t: Even if you seek to harm an enemy, You should remove your own defects and cultivate good qualities. Through that you will help yourself, And the enemy will be displeased.
Even three times a day to offer Three hundred cooking pots of food Does not match a portion of the merit In one instant of love.
If you think you see both Destruction and becoming, Then you see destruction and becoming Through impaired vision.

No suffering is self-caused. Nothing causes itself. If another is not self-made, How could suffering be caused by another? If suffering were caused by each, Suffering could be caused by both. Not caused by self or by other, How could suffering be uncaused?
quotes.c: Mūlamadhyamakakārikā, Mūlamadhyamakakārikā 14.8-9 trans. Jay Garfield, The Fundamental Wisdom of the Middle Way (1995)

quotes.t: The accomplishments of a teacher of ants Are but accomplishments for earning a living. But the study of the termination of earthly incarnation- Why should that not be the accomplishment?
There is pleasure when a sore is scratched, But to be without sores is more pleasurable still. Just so, there are pleasures in worldly desires, But to be without desires is more pleasurable still.

To those possessed of breeding, learning, handsome looks, Who have no wisdom, neither discipline, you need not bow. But those who do have these two qualities, Though lacking other virtues, you should revere.
quotes.c: Suhṛllekha (Letter to a Good Friend), Letter to a Friend (Snow Lion: 2013), stanza 28

quotes.t: Without hope of reward Provide help to others. Bear suffering alone, And share your pleasures with beggars.
All conditioned things are unsatisfactory.
Emptiness is the relinquishing of all views.
The Middle Way avoids the extremes of eternalism and nihilism.
The Middle Way is the path of non-attachment.
The Middle Way is the path of non-conceptualization.
The Tathagata teaches only emptiness.
The antidote to the three poisons is wisdom, compassion, and ethical conduct.
The conventional truth is the truth of dependent origination.
The eightfold path leads to the cessation of suffering.
The four divine abidings of loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity are the path to peace.
The four foundations of mindfulness are the path to liberation.
The four noble truths are the heart of the Buddha's teaching.
The four nutriments of edible food, contact, mental volition, and consciousness sustain the cycle of rebirth.
The four right efforts are the means to overcome the three poisons.
The nature of things is emptiness.
The nature of things is to be devoid of nature.
The one who knows the truth of things knows that all things are interconnected.
The three marks of existence are impermanence, suffering, and non-self.
The three poisons of ignorance, attachment, and aversion cause suffering.
The three trainings of ethics, concentration, and wisdom lead to enlightenment.
The twelve links of dependent origination explain the cycle of rebirth.
The twelve sense bases are the doorways to the cycle of rebirth.
The two truths are not separate, not united.
The ultimate truth is beyond all words and concepts.
The ultimate truth is not a belief, but the absence of all beliefs.
The ultimate truth is not a concept, but the absence of all concepts.
The ultimate truth is not a dogma, but the absence of all dogmas.
The ultimate truth is not a thing, but the absence of all things.
The wise do not assert what they do not know.
The wise do not cling to any view, but see all views as empty.
The wise do not see the world as it appears, but as it is.
The wise do not see the world as permanent, but as constantly changing.
The wise do not see the world as separate, but as one.
The wise do not see the world as solid, but as insubstantial.
The wise understand that all phenomena are empty of inherent existence.
There is no Dharma outside of emptiness.
